title: Lemon-Caper Salmon Piccata with Linguine
dek: Golden salmon fillets sit over silky linguine in a bright lemon-caper pan sauce, giving classic piccata flavors a seafood-forward weeknight format.
image_alt: Golden seared salmon fillets over linguine with lemon slices, capers and a buttery herb-flecked pan sauce
ingredients: 4 center-cut skinless salmon fillets, 5 to 6 oz each and about 1 inch thick
1 tsp kosher salt, divided, plus more for pasta water
1/2 cup dry white wine or low-sodium vegetable broth
1 large lemon, thinly sliced, plus 1 additional lemon for 3 tbsp juice
1/2 cup reserved hot pasta water, as needed

instructions.name: Bring the pasta water to a boil
instructions.text: Bring a large pot of water to a rolling boil. Salt it until pleasantly seasoned, then keep it covered over low heat while the salmon is prepared so the pasta and sauce can finish together.

instructions.name: Dry and season the salmon
instructions.text: Pat the salmon very dry. Season both sides with 3/4 teaspoon kosher salt and the black pepper, then dust the presentation side lightly with flour and shake away every loose patch. The thin coating promotes even browning without creating a breaded crust.

instructions.name: Sear the first side
instructions.text: Heat a 12-inch stainless-steel or cast-iron skillet over medium-high heat for 2 minutes. Add the olive oil and 1 tablespoon butter. When the butter foams, place the salmon flour-side down and cook undisturbed for 3 to 4 minutes, until deeply golden and naturally releasing from the pan.

instructions.name: Finish the salmon safely
instructions.text: Turn the fillets, reduce the heat to medium and cook for 2 to 4 minutes more. Transfer each piece to a clean plate when the thickest center reaches 145°F on an instant-read thermometer. Keep the fish loosely tented; carryover heat will continue cooking it slightly.

instructions.name: Cook the linguine
instructions.text: Add the linguine to the boiling water and cook until just shy of al dente according to the package, usually 9 to 11 minutes. Scoop out 1/2 cup pasta water, then drain thoroughly. Do not rinse away the surface starch that helps the sauce cling.

instructions.name: Deglaze the skillet
instructions.text: Pour off all but 1 tablespoon fat from the skillet. Add the garlic and red pepper flakes over medium heat and stir for 30 seconds. Pour in the wine and scrape up the browned fond; simmer for 2 to 3 minutes, until reduced by roughly half and the raw alcohol aroma has softened.

instructions.name: Build the lemon-caper sauce
instructions.text: Add the broth, lemon slices, capers and remaining 1/4 teaspoon salt. Simmer for 3 minutes. Reduce the heat to low, add the remaining 3 tablespoons cold butter one piece at a time and swirl until glossy. Stir in 3 tablespoons lemon juice. Do not boil after adding the butter or the sauce may split.

instructions.name: Coat the linguine
instructions.text: Add the drained linguine, Parmesan and half the parsley to the skillet. Toss for 1 to 2 minutes, adding reserved pasta water a tablespoon at a time until the sauce forms a fluid coating around the noodles rather than pooling or turning greasy.

instructions.name: Plate like the photograph
instructions.text: Divide the sauced linguine among four warm shallow bowls. Set one salmon fillet over each portion, spoon capers and lemon sauce across the fish and finish with the remaining parsley. Serve immediately while the sauce is emulsified and the salmon is hot.

why_it_works: Dry salmon and a whisper-thin flour coating create the evenly golden surface that anchors the buttery sauce without turning the fish heavy.
Reducing wine against the skillet fond builds savory depth, while lemon juice added after the butter keeps the sauce bright and balanced.
Starchy pasta water and finely grated Parmesan bridge the pan sauce and linguine, producing a glossy coating rather than separate oil and broth.
swaps: Use four 5-ounce skinless cod or halibut fillets and cook to 145°F; thinner pieces will finish sooner than the salmon.
Replace the wine with additional low-sodium vegetable broth plus 1 teaspoon white wine vinegar added with the lemon juice.
Spaghetti or fettuccine can replace linguine; use the package timing and still reserve starchy cooking water before draining.
storage: Refrigerate salmon and sauced linguine in separate shallow airtight containers within 2 hours for up to 3 days. Reheat the pasta gently in a skillet with a splash of broth until steaming, then warm the salmon covered in a 300°F oven to 165°F. Freezing is not recommended because the emulsified sauce can split and the fish becomes dry.
notes: Center-cut fillets of similar thickness finish together. If one reaches 145°F early, remove it rather than waiting for the others.
Capers vary in saltiness. Drain brined capers well and season the finished sauce only after they have simmered.
Cold butter incorporated over low heat is essential for a glossy piccata sauce; high heat turns the butter oily and dull.

faqs.q: Why did my salmon stick to the skillet?
faqs.a: The pan or oil was probably not fully hot, the salmon surface was damp or the fish was turned too soon. Dry it thoroughly, preheat the skillet for 2 minutes and wait until the browned side releases with only gentle pressure.

faqs.q: Can I make salmon piccata without pasta?
faqs.a: Yes. Omit the linguine, halve the Parmesan and pasta water, and serve the salmon and sauce with roasted potatoes, polenta or crusty bread. The fish and sauce method stays the same.

faqs.q: How do I keep the lemon-caper sauce from breaking?
faqs.a: Reduce the wine and broth before adding butter, lower the heat and swirl in cold butter gradually. Once emulsified, keep the sauce below a simmer and loosen it with warm pasta water instead of more oil.

title: Sheet-Pan Sweet Potato & Mushroom Fajitas with Guacamole
dek: Smoky roasted sweet potato, mushrooms, corn and red onion fill warm tortillas with quick lime guacamole for a colorful, substantial meatless dinner.
image_alt: Soft flour tortillas filled with roasted sweet potato, mushrooms, corn, red onion and cilantro beside a bowl of green guacamole and lime wedges
ingredients: 1 large sweet potato, about 1 lb, peeled and cut into 1/2-inch-thick sticks
12 oz cremini mushrooms, wiped clean and sliced 1/3 inch thick
1 medium red onion, halved and sliced into 1/3-inch wedges
1 red bell pepper, cored and cut into 1/2-inch strips
1 cup frozen corn kernels, thawed and patted dry
1/4 cup finely chopped cilantro, plus whole leaves for serving

instructions.name: Heat two sheet pans
instructions.text: Arrange racks in the upper and lower thirds of the oven and heat to 450°F with two heavy rimmed sheet pans inside. Preheating the metal starts browning the vegetables immediately and prevents a soft, steamed surface.

instructions.name: Season the sweet potato
instructions.text: In a large bowl, toss the sweet potato with 1 tablespoon olive oil, 1 teaspoon cumin, 3/4 teaspoon smoked paprika, 1/2 teaspoon chili powder, 1/4 teaspoon oregano, 1/4 teaspoon salt and half the black pepper. Keep the sticks in a single layer so their edges caramelize.

instructions.name: Season the remaining vegetables
instructions.text: In a second bowl, toss the mushrooms, red onion, bell pepper and dry corn with 1 1/2 tablespoons olive oil, the remaining cumin, smoked paprika, chili powder, oregano, 1/2 teaspoon salt and black pepper. Coating the vegetables separately prevents the sweet potato from breaking.

instructions.name: Start the sweet potato
instructions.text: Carefully remove one hot pan with heat-safe mitts. Spread the sweet potato in one layer and roast on the lower rack for 10 minutes. Leave space around the pieces and return the pan to the oven promptly.

instructions.name: Roast the fajita vegetables
instructions.text: Spread the mushroom mixture across the second hot pan. Roast both pans for 12 minutes, placing the mushrooms on the upper rack. Rotate the pans and turn the sweet potatoes, then roast for 6 to 8 minutes more, until the potatoes are tender with dark edges and the mushrooms are browned rather than watery.

instructions.name: Make the lime guacamole
instructions.text: While the vegetables roast, mash the avocados with the juice of 1 lime, the grated garlic, chopped cilantro and remaining 1/2 teaspoon salt. Leave some small avocado pieces for texture. Press reusable wrap directly against the surface if it must wait longer than 10 minutes.

instructions.name: Brighten the roasted filling
instructions.text: Combine the contents of both pans, drizzle with the remaining 1/2 tablespoon olive oil and squeeze over half of the second lime. Toss gently and taste. The filling should be smoky, well salted and bright enough to stand up to the tortillas.

instructions.name: Warm the tortillas safely
instructions.text: Stack the tortillas, wrap them tightly in foil and warm in the switched-off oven for 5 minutes. Alternatively, warm each tortilla for about 20 seconds per side in a dry skillet until flexible; never place tortillas directly over an unattended gas flame.

instructions.name: Assemble the fajitas
instructions.text: Spread guacamole in each warm tortilla, then add sweet potato, mushrooms, corn, bell pepper and red onion. Finish with cilantro leaves, jalapeño and pickled onions if using. Serve with the remaining lime wedges while the vegetables are hot.

why_it_works: Preheated pans and a 450°F oven drive off surface moisture quickly, giving mushrooms and sweet potatoes browned edges instead of a watery roast.
Sweet potato starts alone because it needs more time; the quicker-cooking mushrooms, pepper, onion and corn retain distinct textures.
Creamy lime guacamole supplies richness and acidity, making the vegetable filling satisfying without cheese or meat.
swaps: Use peeled butternut squash cut into 1/2-inch sticks instead of sweet potato; begin checking it after 20 total minutes.
Replace cremini mushrooms with sliced portobello caps or oyster mushrooms, keeping the pieces broad enough to brown rather than shrivel.
Corn tortillas make the meal gluten-free only when the package is certified gluten-free; warm them individually so they remain flexible.
storage: Cool the roasted vegetables promptly and refrigerate them separately from tortillas and guacamole within 2 hours for up to 4 days. Press wrap against the guacamole and use within 2 days. Reheat the filling on a sheet pan at 425°F for 8 to 10 minutes or in a skillet until steaming; warm tortillas separately. Freeze the roasted filling for up to 2 months, but do not freeze the guacamole.
notes: Mushrooms absorb rinse water. Wipe them clean and keep the slices fairly thick so they brown and remain visible in the finished fajitas.
Frozen corn must be thawed and dried before roasting; wet kernels cool the pan and steam the surrounding vegetables.
If only one sheet pan is available, roast the sweet potato first, transfer it to a plate and roast the remaining vegetables second rather than crowding everything together.

faqs.q: Why are my sheet-pan fajita vegetables soggy?
faqs.a: The pans may not have been preheated, the vegetables may be wet or the pieces may be crowded. Use two hot heavy pans, dry the corn and mushrooms well and keep every component in a loose single layer.

faqs.q: Can I prepare the vegetables ahead?
faqs.a: Yes. Cut and season the sweet potato up to 1 day ahead and refrigerate it airtight. Slice the mushrooms, pepper and onion up to 1 day ahead, but keep them dry and toss with oil and spices just before roasting.

faqs.q: How can I add more protein to vegetarian fajitas?
faqs.a: Add one drained 15-ounce can of black beans during the final 8 minutes of roasting, or serve the fajitas with 2 cups warmed seasoned black beans on the side. Either option keeps the meal meatless.

title: Cinnamon-Sugar Pumpkin Mini Muffins
dek: Tender orange-crumb pumpkin mini muffins get a warm butter dip and complete cinnamon-sugar coating for a crisp, sparkling finish and soft spiced center.
image_alt: Small orange pumpkin muffins coated all over in sparkling cinnamon sugar, with one cut open to show the tender spiced crumb
ingredients: Nonstick baking spray, for the pan
3/4 cup packed light brown sugar, 150 g
1/2 cup neutral oil, such as avocado or canola
1/4 cup whole milk, at room temperature
4 tbsp unsalted butter, melted, for coating
1/2 cup granulated sugar, 100 g, for coating

instructions.name: Prepare the oven and pan
instructions.text: Heat the oven to 375°F with a rack in the center. Coat two 12-cup mini-muffin pans thoroughly with nonstick spray, including the flat surface around the wells. If baking in batches, cool and clean the pan before regreasing it.

instructions.name: Whisk the dry mixture
instructions.text: In a medium bowl, whisk the flour, baking powder, baking soda, 1 1/2 teaspoons cinnamon, ginger, nutmeg, cloves and salt for 30 seconds. Breaking up every spice pocket now prevents bitter streaks in the small muffins.

instructions.name: Mix the pumpkin base
instructions.text: In a large bowl, whisk the brown sugar and eggs until smooth and slightly lightened, about 45 seconds. Whisk in the pumpkin, oil, milk and vanilla until the mixture is uniform with no visible egg streaks.

instructions.name: Fold the batter gently
instructions.text: Add the dry mixture to the pumpkin mixture. Fold with a flexible spatula just until no dry flour remains, scraping the bottom and sides once. Stop immediately; overmixing develops gluten and makes mini muffins rubbery.

instructions.name: Portion evenly
instructions.text: Divide the batter among 24 mini-muffin wells, filling each about three-quarters full with roughly 1 1/2 tablespoons batter. Wipe drips from the top of the pan so they do not burn.

instructions.name: Bake to precise doneness
instructions.text: Bake for 11 to 14 minutes, rotating the pans front to back after 8 minutes, until the tops spring back, a tester carries only a few moist crumbs and the center of a muffin registers 200 to 205°F. Avoid baking until completely dry.

instructions.name: Release and cool briefly
instructions.text: Rest the muffins in the pans for 5 minutes. Run a thin flexible spatula around any stuck edges and transfer the muffins to a wire rack for 3 minutes. They should be warm enough to absorb a little butter but firm enough to handle.

instructions.name: Make the cinnamon sugar
instructions.text: While the muffins cool, place the melted butter in one shallow bowl. In a second shallow bowl, stir the granulated sugar with the remaining 1 1/2 teaspoons cinnamon until the color is completely even.

instructions.name: Coat every muffin
instructions.text: Working one at a time, brush or roll each warm muffin lightly in melted butter, letting excess drip away, then roll it in cinnamon sugar to coat the top, sides and base. Set on the rack for 10 minutes so the sparkling crust adheres before serving.

why_it_works: Oil and pumpkin purée keep the small crumb tender even after the muffins cool, while room-temperature eggs and milk blend without tightening the batter.
Baking powder and baking soda work together against pumpkin's density, producing rounded tops and an open but sturdy orange crumb.
A light butter layer applied while warm anchors cinnamon sugar over the entire muffin, creating the distinct sparkling shell shown in the finished bake.
swaps: Use 1 3/4 teaspoons pumpkin pie spice in place of the cinnamon, ginger, nutmeg and cloves in the batter; keep the separate cinnamon-sugar coating unchanged.
Unsweetened applesauce can replace the oil by volume, but the muffins will be softer, less rich and best eaten the day they are baked.
For 12 standard muffins, fill greased wells three-quarters full and bake at 375°F for 18 to 22 minutes, checking for a 200 to 205°F center.
storage: Let the coated muffins cool completely, then keep them in a loosely covered container at room temperature for up to 2 days; airtight storage softens the sugar crust. Refrigerate for up to 5 days and rewarm at 300°F for 5 minutes. Freeze uncoated baked muffins for up to 2 months, thaw at room temperature, warm briefly and add fresh butter and cinnamon sugar before serving.
notes: Use canned pure pumpkin, not sweetened pumpkin pie filling, which would make the batter overly sweet and alter the liquid balance.
Mini-muffin pans vary in depth. Portion by volume and begin checking at 11 minutes rather than relying only on the clock.
For a neat rather than greasy coating, brush on a very thin butter film or roll quickly and let each muffin drip before it enters the sugar.

faqs.q: Why did my pumpkin mini muffins turn dense?
faqs.a: The batter was likely overmixed, the leaveners may be old or too much flour was packed into cups. Weigh 219 grams flour, whisk fresh leaveners through the dry ingredients and fold only until the last flour streak disappears.

faqs.q: Can I coat the muffins ahead of time?
faqs.a: They are crispest within 4 hours of coating. For next-day serving, bake and cool the muffins, store them uncoated, then warm at 300°F for 4 minutes and apply melted butter and fresh cinnamon sugar.

faqs.q: How do I keep mini muffins from sticking?
faqs.a: Use a fresh, thorough layer of baking spray, including the top rim, and rest the baked muffins for exactly 5 minutes before loosening them. Too little grease causes sticking, while cooling fully in the pan traps steam and weakens the sides.
